newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gives Jordan special status.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives Jordan special status.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has named Jordan a major non-NATO ally of the United States, entitling the kingdom to "priority consideration" for military aid and equipment, the State Department said on Thursday.

"Effective Nov. 13, 1996, the president designated Jordan a major non-NATO ally of the United States, pursuant to section 517 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961," deputy spokesman Glyn Davies told reporters.

He said the new status "makes Jordan eligible for priority consideration for the transfer of excess defence articles, the use of already appropriated military assistance funds for procurement through commercial leases, the stockpiling of U.S. military material and the purchase of depleted uranium munitions."
The spokesman said he did not believe the designation carried with it any new or expanded U.S. commitment to come to Jordan's defence in a time of crisis.
The special status was warranted because of Jordan's place in the Middle East and U.S.-led peacemaking there.

"This designation reflects that Jordan plays a key role in an area of strategic interest to the United States (and) that Jordan has joined Egypt and Israel as a full partner in the effort to bring peace to the Middle East," Davies said.

U.S. relations with Jordan plummeted during the 1991 Gulf War when the kingdom was sympathetic with Iraq. But ties improved dramatically after Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in October, 1994.
Since then, Washington has taken several steps to strengthen ties with Jordan, including the transfer of an F-16 squadron to Jordan.
Jordan maintains a wide range of U.S. military systems and technology.
"In essence this new designation recognises Jordan's continued support for peace and underscores the strong relationship that's growing between Jordan and the United States," Davies said.
Other countries that have also been granted this status are Australia, Egypt, Israel, Japan and the Republic of Korea.
